conclusion.justification: The report concludes that the claim is not established as a general rule, noting that current evidence does not reliably show vegetarians live longer than comparable meat-eaters and citing studies showing similar all-cause mortality.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
**Conclusion:** The claim is **not established as a general rule**. Vegetarian diets can be healthy and may lower risks for some chronic diseases, but current evidence does not show reliably that vegetarians live longer than comparable meat-eaters.

The key evidence is observational, so it can show associations—not prove that avoiding meat causes longer life. In Adventist Health Study-2, vegetarian dietary patterns were associated with lower mortality, but Adventists also differ from the general population in lifestyle and health behaviors, making residual confounding possible. https://archive.connect.h1.co/article/718113551/

Importantly, a large UK analysis designed to compare vegetarians with relatively health-conscious nonvegetarians concluded that they had **similar all-cause mortality**. That directly conflicts with the broad life-expectancy claim, though differences for particular causes of death remained uncertain. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4691673/

There is good reason to favor plant-rich eating and to limit particular meats: WHO/IARC finds processed meat carcinogenic and red meat probably carcinogenic, but explicitly says this assessment **did not directly compare** health risks of vegetarian and meat-eating diets. https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/cancer-carcinogenicity-of-the-consumption-of-red-meat-and-processed-meat

A well-planned vegetarian (including vegan) diet is considered nutritionally adequate and may help prevent or treat some diseases—but that is not evidence of longer life. https://www.jandonline.org/article/S2212-2672(16)31192-3/fulltext

**Bottom line:** Replacing processed/red meat with minimally processed plant foods is plausibly beneficial; “being vegetarian” alone does not currently demonstrate a longer life expectancy.
